facts.content: Patient presents with a 3-day history of diarrhea and vomiting.
facts.source_text: CC: 3-day history of diarrhea and vomiting

facts.content: Diarrhea began as watery and is now very loose, with at least four stools today.
facts.source_text: Diarrhea: started watery, now very loose; ≥4 stools today

facts.content: Patient has had multiple episodes of vomiting and cannot keep fluids or tea down.
facts.source_text: Vomiting: multiple episodes; cannot keep fluids/tea down

facts.content: The last episode of vomiting occurred approximately this morning after breakfast.
facts.source_text: last emesis ~this morning after breakfast

facts.content: Patient reports a subjective fever described as 'literally boiling' without a thermometer reading.
facts.source_text: Subjective fever/"literally boiling"; no thermometer reading

facts.content: Patient reports periumbilical abdominal pain that is tender to touch and intermittent with the urge to defecate.
facts.source_text: Abdominal pain: periumbilical, tender to touch, intermittent with urge to defecate

facts.content: Patient passed urine about one hour ago with no visible blood.
facts.source_text: Urine: passed ~1 hr ago; no visible blood

facts.content: Patient reports no blood in stool.
facts.source_text: No blood in stool reported

facts.content: Patient reports exposure to a brother with similar symptoms and an outbreak at school.
facts.source_text: Exposure: brother with similar symptoms; household contact; reports outbreak at school

facts.content: Patient has been using oral rehydration solution made from salt and sugar approximately three times per day for two days, but vomiting limits its effectiveness.
facts.source_text: Self-treatment: ORS (salt/sugar mix) ~3x/day x2 days; vomiting limits effectiveness

facts.content: Patient reports menstrual cramps as the only past medical history.
facts.source_text: PMH: menstrual cramps only

facts.content: Patient takes Vitamin D daily.
facts.source_text: Meds: Vitamin D daily

facts.content: Patient uses 'naprine' as needed for menstrual cramps as reported by the patient.
facts.source_text: Meds: Vitamin D daily; "naprine" PRN for cramps (patient report)

facts.content: Patient is a non-smoker.
facts.source_text: SH: Non-smoker

facts.content: Patient drinks alcohol occasionally, sometimes a pint.
facts.source_text: occasional alcohol (a pint sometimes)

facts.content: Patient works as a graphics designer and is working from home today.
facts.source_text: graphics designer; working from home today

facts.content: Patient lives with her brother and mother.
facts.source_text: lives with brother and mother

facts.content: Patient is not sexually active and is not using contraception.
facts.source_text: Sexual/contraception: not sexually active; not on contraception

facts.content: Acute infectious gastroenteritis is diagnosed, considered likely viral given household and school contacts and three days of watery diarrhea and vomiting.
facts.source_text: 1. Acute infectious gastroenteritis — likely viral given household/school contacts; 3 days of watery diarrhea and vomiting

facts.content: There is a risk of dehydration due to persistent vomiting and poor oral intake.
facts.source_text: 2. Risk of dehydration due to persistent vomiting and poor oral intake

facts.content: Patient has periumbilical abdominal pain that is intermittent and associated with stooling.
facts.source_text: 3. Periumbilical abdominal pain, intermittent, associated with stooling

facts.content: Patient is assessed as having a subjective fever.
facts.source_text: 4. Subjective fever

facts.content: Plan is to arrange an urgent clinic appointment via the support line for stool specimen collection and hydration assessment, with the patient agreeing to have the appointment booked.
facts.source_text: Arrange urgent clinic appointment via support line for stool specimen collection and hydration assessment (patient agreed; appointment to be booked)

facts.content: If the patient is seen, a stool sample will be sent for culture and MC&S to exclude bacterial pathogens, and targeted therapy will be considered if a bacterial cause is identified.
facts.source_text: If seen, send stool sample for culture/MC&S to exclude bacterial pathogens; consider targeted therapy if bacterial cause identified

facts.content: Patient is advised to continue oral rehydration solution in very small, frequent sips and to attempt oral rehydration even if nauseated, avoiding large boluses.
facts.source_text: Continue ORS in very small, frequent sips; attempt oral rehydration even if nausea — avoid large boluses

facts.content: Dietary advice is to eat bland, light foods such as toast or biscuits and to avoid fruit, vegetables, and milk while symptomatic.
facts.source_text: Diet: bland, light foods (e.g., toast/biscuits); avoid fruit, vegetables, milk while symptomatic

facts.content: If the patient is unable to retain oral rehydration solution, or has worsening tachypnea, oliguria, dizziness, or overall clinical deterioration, she is instructed to attend A&E for intravenous fluids and urgent care.
facts.source_text: If unable to retain ORS, worsening tachypnea/oliguria/dizziness, or clinical deterioration → attend A&E for IV fluids and urgent care

facts.content: Safety-net advice is for the patient to call back or present to A&E if symptoms worsen before the clinic appointment.
facts.source_text: Safety-net: patient to call back or present to A&E if symptoms worsen before clinic appointment
